summary: This informational memo documents the parameters used in MAPOS version 1, the Multiple Access Protocol over SONET/SDH.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2172 is a short reference list. MAPOS is a way for many computers to share a fast optical network link, and each frame carries a number that says what kind of data is inside. This memo records which numbers are already assigned, so implementers use the same ones.

questions: what is the mapos ipv4 protocol number
subtitle: The registry of Protocol field values used by MAPOS version 1, a multiple-access link layer for SONET/SDH.

tldr.problem: MAPOS version 1 frames carry a 16-bit Protocol field, and every implementation needs the same list of which values mean what.
tldr.mechanism: The memo lists the assigned values, such as 0021 for IPv4 and FE01 for ARP, and states a rule about the least significant bit of each octet.
tldr.outcome: It is a short reference for implementers of MAPOS version 1. It is not a standards-track document and not an IETF working group product.

today: RFC 2172 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The protocol itself is defined in RFC 2171.

sections.title: What MAPOS Is
sections.content:
MAPOS (Multiple Access Protocol over SONET/SDH) is a high-speed link-layer protocol that provides multiple access over SONET (Synchronous Optical Network) and SDH (Synchronous Digital Hierarchy) links. Its frame format is based on the HDLC-like framing used for PPP. A component called a Frame Switch lets multiple nodes connect in a star topology to form a LAN, and over long-haul SONET/SDH links such a network can span a wide geographic area. IP datagrams are transmitted in MAPOS HDLC frames.

The authors' note says the document is not the product of an IETF working group, is not a standards-track document, and has not necessarily had the in-depth community review that standards-track documents receive. It documents the parameters of MAPOS version 1.
sections.plainLanguage: MAPOS lets several computers share one fast fiber-optic line through a central switch. This memo is only a lookup table of the numeric tags its frames use.

sections.title: The Protocol Field Rule
sections.content: The MAPOS version 1 data link layer contains a 16-bit Protocol field that identifies the encapsulated protocol. The field follows the ISO 3309 (HDLC) extension mechanism for address fields. All protocol numbers MUST be assigned so that the least significant bit of the most significant octet is 0 and the least significant bit of the least significant octet is 1.
sections.plainLanguage: Every protocol tag follows one bit pattern, so a receiver always knows that the first byte is not the end and the last byte is. This keeps the numbers unambiguous.

sections.title: Assigned Protocol Numbers
sections.content: The memo gives the assigned values in hexadecimal. 0021 is MAPOS Version 1 Internet Protocol Version 4, defined in RFC 2176. FE01 is the Address Resolution Protocol. FE03 is the Node Switch Protocol, defined in RFC 2173. FE05 is the Switch Switch Protocol, defined in RFC 2174. The ranges 0001-001F, 0023-FCFF and FE07-FEFF are marked not used and reserved.
sections.plainLanguage: A few numbers are taken: one for internet data, one for finding a machine's address, and two for jobs the switches do. The rest are saved for later use.
